$Comment: Bram the Shepherd, one of the three villagers standing in the Forgotten Temple while Harvest Feast
runs, so a player carrying the invitation tour always has somebody to ask, and one of Santa's three
helpers while Christmas runs. The roles, this placement and the conversations pressing F opens all
ship in this pack. Author Dialogue or Open, never both.
Seasons is what makes Bram a guest, and one man in two seasons: the placement stands while any listed
calendar event is switched on and running, and the entry in effect is the first, in list order, whose
event runs. The Harvest_Feast entry comes first and changes nothing, so while the feast runs (its last
days overlap the start of Christmas) he wears his feast clothes and speaks his feast conversation,
which gains a Christmas line from the first day of Christmas
(DialogueExtensions/SeasonsOfOrbis/Christmas_Shepherd_Feast_Line.json). Once only Christmas runs, its
entry replaces two leaves whole: Role, his winter clothes (NPC/Roles/Passive/Christmas_Shepherd.json),
the library changing the standing NPC's role in place, and Interact, his Christmas conversation
(Dialogues/SeasonsOfOrbis/Christmas_Shepherd.json). It writes no Anchor, so he keeps his meadow in both
seasons. The library looks at every placement again at each start and end and whenever he is loaded,
so nothing needs a restart. Lifecycle keeps his chunk loaded, stands him up again if something removes
him, and raises his health past anything that can be dealt.
Where finds the temple by its GameplayConfig id, which stays the same on every visit while the
world's name does not. Identity.NpcId is spelled as his feast role and never changes with an entry's
Role, so a nameplate key built from it resolves and every quest, talk step and hand-in bound to
Harvest_Feast_Shepherd finds him in both seasons. Each villager has an id and a conversation of their
own: the invitation line is spent per conversation, so two villagers sharing one would count as one
person asked.
The three villagers stand apart at the feast, so asking them all is a walk through the temple: Bram
on the meadow halfway down the road from the arrival, Tomas where that road comes into the kweebec
village, and Elsie on the village's far side. No spawn marker stands on that meadow, so Anchor is the
temple's arrival spot plus an offset, as the host's is: fifty and a half blocks along negative X down
the road, eight down (the road falls eight blocks from the landing to the meadow, and an anchor never
finds the ground for itself), and eleven along positive Z, off the road onto the grass. To move Bram,
edit Anchor.WorldSpawn.Offset and Yaw, keeping Y on the ground the new spot stands on, then look at
the spot in game. To take him out without editing this file, set enabled (lower case, as that file
spells it) to false for this id in mods/ziggfreedcommon/npc-placements.json.
Name: Harvest_Feast_Shepherd_Temple
